Perfect! **The design is now fixed and all tests pass.**

The bugs I fixed were:

1. **Missing counter reset condition**: When `din == dout`, the stability counter must be cleared to 0 (per spec), but the original code had no else clause to handle this. I added the proper else block.

2. **Off-by-one timing error**: The original code checked `if (cnt == N)` after incrementing, causing the output to toggle at the (N+1)-th edge instead of the N-th edge. I restructured it to increment first (`cnt <= cnt + 8'd1`) then check `if (cnt + 8'd1 == N)` to ensure the output changes at exactly the right time.

The fixed implementation now correctly implements the counter-based debouncer behavior specified: the output changes exactly when the input has differed from the output for N consecutive clock edges.
